features.heading: Features
features.noSubscriptions.title: One Price, Yours for Good
features.noSubscriptions.body: Pay US$3.99 once and keep ShortcutCycle. No subscription and no recurring fees.
features.groups.title: Apps grouped by task
features.groups.body: Put apps for coding, writing, or keeping in touch into separate groups. Switch only between the apps you need for that task.
features.switching.title: Instant Switching
features.switching.body: Tap to switch or hold to preview. Set a one-app group to use running apps only, then use its shortcut to bring the app forward and hide it again.
features.profiles.title: Browser Profiles
features.profiles.body: When Chrome, Firefox, or Edge runs profiles as separate instances, ShortcutCycle keeps work and personal profiles distinct.
features.hud.title: Preview before switching
features.hud.body: A simple preview shows the selected app before you switch, so you know where you are going.
features.native.title: At Home on Your Mac
features.native.body: Opens quickly, stays out of the Dock, and feels like part of macOS.
features.launch.title: Each Group, Your Way
features.launch.body: Choose whether a group includes only apps already open or can open the next app for you.
features.privacy.title: Private by Design
features.privacy.body: No analytics or tracking. Your groups and shortcuts stay on your Mac, and you can export a copy whenever you want.
features.backups.title: Automatic Backups
features.backups.body: ShortcutCycle quietly saves earlier setups, so an accidental change is easy to undo.
features.automation.title: Fits Your Automation
features.automation.body: Connect your groups to Apple Shortcuts, Alfred, Raycast, Keyboard Maestro, or shell scripts. Explore automation commands.
features.global.title: Your Language, Built In

faq.title: Frequently Asked Questions
faq.gettingStarted.title: Getting Started
faq.gettingStarted.createQuestion: How do I create a group?
faq.gettingStarted.createAnswer: Open Settings, click +, and name a group such as "Social" or "Dev." Add apps that are running now or browse for others, then press the shortcut you want, such as Option+1.
faq.gettingStarted.shortcutsAnswer: Yes. Press the combination you want. ShortcutCycle suggests recent choices and warns if one is already in use. Add Command, Control, or Option to letter and number keys; function keys can work on their own.
faq.gettingStarted.closedAppQuestion: What happens if an app isn't open?
faq.gettingStarted.closedAppAnswer: The group's mode decides. Running Apps Only skips closed apps while any group app is running; if none are running, it launches the first app. All Apps launches a closed app when selected.
faq.automation.title: Automation
faq.automation.toolsQuestion: Can I automate ShortcutCycle with Shortcuts, Alfred, or Raycast?
faq.automation.toolsAnswerIntro: Yes. Connect a group to the automation tools you already use. For example:
faq.automation.openQuestion: Can automation open Settings or my backups?
faq.automation.importQuestion: Can I automate setup transfers or backup restores?
faq.automation.importAnswerIntro: Yes. Automation can save or load a setup and bring back a backup. For example:
faq.automation.importAnswerTail: ShortcutCycle checks an incoming setup before replacing anything. If it cannot be used safely, your current groups and settings stay unchanged.
faq.privacy.title: Backups & Privacy
faq.privacy.backupQuestion: Can I back up my setup?
faq.privacy.backupAnswer: Yes. ShortcutCycle automatically keeps a useful history of earlier setups. You can also export a copy whenever you want to keep one elsewhere or move it to another Mac.
faq.privacy.privateAnswer: Yes. ShortcutCycle runs entirely on your Mac with no analytics or tracking. Your app groups and shortcuts stay on your Mac; we never see or collect them.
faq.compatibility.title: Compatibility & Project
faq.compatibility.monitorsQuestion: Does it work with multiple monitors?
faq.compatibility.monitorsAnswer: Yes. The switching preview appears on the display you are using, and you can switch to an app on any connected display.
faq.compatibility.windowQuestion: Why doesn't ShortcutCycle switch to a specific window?
faq.compatibility.windowAnswer: ShortcutCycle switches apps rather than individual windows. That keeps its permissions limited while making app-group switching fast and dependable.
faq.compatibility.openSourceAnswer: Yes! ShortcutCycle is 100% open source under the MIT license. You can view the code, contribute, or build it yourself on GitHub.

privacy.meta.title: Privacy Policy — ShortcutCycle
privacy.meta.description: How ShortcutCycle handles your information and permissions.
privacy.title: Privacy Policy
privacy.intro: ShortcutCycle (“we,” “us,” or “our”) respects your privacy. This Privacy Policy describes how we collect, use, and handle your information when you use our application.
privacy.collection.title: Data collection
privacy.collection.summary: We do not collect, store, or transmit any of your personal data.
privacy.collection.body: ShortcutCycle is a localized macOS utility that operates entirely on your device.
privacy.tracking: No tracking: We do not track your usage or usage patterns.
privacy.analytics: No analytics: We do not use third-party analytics services.
privacy.accounts: No accounts: You do not need to create an account to use the app.
privacy.permissions.title: Permissions
privacy.permissions.body: ShortcutCycle registers the keyboard shortcuts you assign and uses standard macOS features to switch between apps. When you import or export settings, you choose which settings files the app can access.
privacy.contact.title: Contact us
privacy.contact.body: If you have questions about this Privacy Policy, visit our Support page to contact us.
support.meta.title: Support — ShortcutCycle
support.meta.description: Get help with app groups, shortcuts, and backups in ShortcutCycle.
support.title: Support
support.intro: Find help for your shortcuts, app groups, and backups.
support.menuBar.question: Where is ShortcutCycle after I open it?
support.menuBar.answer: ShortcutCycle lives in the menu bar, so it does not appear in the Dock. Click its menu bar icon to open Settings and manage your groups.
support.shortcuts.question: Why is my shortcut not working?
support.shortcuts.answer: Check that the group is enabled and has a shortcut assigned. If the combination is already used by another group, app, or macOS, choose a different one.
support.report.title: Report a bug or suggest a feature
support.report.body: Share your feedback through GitHub Issues.
support.report.include: Include your ShortcutCycle and macOS versions, what you expected, and the steps to reproduce the issue.
support.report.destination: Opens GitHub in a new tab. A GitHub account is needed to submit an issue.
